reasons: Historical recovery materially improves architecture continuity but is not new empirical support.
Delta overlay, epoch consistency and lazy latent-field results are synthetic Python proxies rather than actual current-corpus runtime evidence.
The central new claim—memory state influences the next model decision beneficially before explicit retrieval—has not yet been tested under matched visible-information controls.
Target Qwen-class 4B, concurrent live/twin FRANK, 71-store parity/p99/crash/privacy and stale-frame tests remain open.
positive_evidence: Older Clay/XENO/ClayCode research already specified incremental relations, activation budget/inhibition, Assembly lifecycle and physically plural logical state; G1d restores these without reviving retired claims.
30k-node proxy showed delta overlays preserve query results across tested update sizes and can avoid full rebuild cost for small changes; workload determines crossover.
1,000 pinned old/new epoch queries produced zero mismatches in the local snapshot proxy.
Sparse lazy latent activation reduced median synthetic event-update cost from 1.098 ms eager whole-field decay to 0.028 ms while final active set remained about 5.2% of nodes.
Current external research independently explores spreading activation, dynamic graph memory, incremental memory and bitemporal agent memory.
next_gates: implement immutable base+delta epochs on actual current ClayGraph corpus
concurrent publish/read/crash/reclamation stress with deterministic replay
implement sparse latent field with saturation/inhibition and measure long-run active fraction/noise
matched no-field vs truthful-field vs shuffled-field 4B experiment with equal final visible facts/order/token budget
test events where query-only retrieval fails to initiate memory lookup
measure workload-adaptive compaction controller vs fixed incremental/rebuild policies
